article.title: NFL EDGE Sunday Evening Brief
article.dek: Both morning cards hit, the 6pm board has two Broncos plays for tonight, and the Hit Rate card goes quiet.

items.headline: Sunday night: two Broncos plays, one missing star
paragraphs: Rams at Broncos kicks off at 6:20 p.m. MDT on NBC, and the 6 p.m. board has two plays on it - both on Denver. Balanced is Broncos moneyline at -102 on FanDuel. Value is Broncos +1.5 at -120 on DraftKings. There is no Hit Rate card tonight.

The personnel news is all on the inactive lists. Rams star receiver Puka Nacua (hip) is out, and so is safety Kam Kinchens. Tight end Colby Parkinson (knee) is active. For Denver, receiver Marvin Mims (foot) is out, rookie running back Jonah Coleman went to injured reserve Saturday with an ankle injury, and Tyler Badie is the third back behind J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey.

The market spent the day moving toward Denver: the Rams went from -130 to -112 on the DraftKings moneyline, and Denver went from +110 to -108 (-102 on FanDuel). The Nacua news is the day's obvious backdrop. The app's expected-margin number still has the Rams by less than a point - basically a pick'em - and the evening cards are priced on the moved number, not the morning one.
items.takeaway: Two Denver plays at kickoff. No Hit Rate card.

items.headline: Sunday's injury and quarterback news, all in one place
paragraphs: The new one: Miami running back De'Von Achane hurt his knee on the Dolphins' opening drive against Kansas City and was ruled out. He managed 17 yards on three carries before leaving with trainers' help. Miami goes to Minnesota next week.
Tonight's game: Puka Nacua (hip) and Kam Kinchens (hamstring) out for the Rams; Marvin Mims (foot) out for Denver; Jonah Coleman (ankle) to injured reserve, out at least four games.
Elsewhere today: Panthers receiver Jalen Coker left with a groin injury and did not return; Tampa Bay's Baker Mayfield hurt his hand late in the loss to Minnesota.

Monday night: Caleb Williams (hamstring) is out for Chicago. Tyson Bagent cleared the concussion protocol Saturday, practiced in full, and coach Ben Johnson says he'll be available - Bagent is officially questionable but the expected starter, and the app agrees. Case Keenum is the fallback. For Philadelphia, tight end Dallas Goedert (knee), receiver Marquise Brown (ankle), and tackle Fred Johnson (knee) are out; linebacker Jonathan Greenard (pectoral) is questionable. Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith practiced fully Saturday and carry no designation.
items.takeaway: Achane's knee is the new one to watch. Everything else is as expected.

items.headline: The morning cards both hit
paragraphs: Giants 12, Titans 7. The nor'easter game went the way the cards said: Giants moneyline at -130 was the Hit Rate and Balanced play, and it cashed. Jameis Winston managed the weather, rookie kicker Dominic Zvada hit all four field goals, and Jevon Holland's end-zone interception with 17 seconds left sealed it. Cam Ward threw for 181 yards and a touchdown but took the loss on that final pick.

Raiders 35, Saints 27. The Value card - Raiders moneyline at +164 - hit too. Kirk Cousins threw three touchdowns, Brock Bowers returned from knee surgery with 10 catches for 116 yards and a score, and the Saints turned it over four times in the fourth quarter. Las Vegas is 3-0.

The rest of the afternoon: Washington 33, Seattle 31 - Marcus Mariota threw three touchdowns in relief of Jayden Daniels, Sam Darnold threw for 379 yards and four scores but also two interceptions including a fourth-quarter pick-six, and Seattle's 12-game winning streak is over. Kansas City 24, Miami 10 - the Chiefs covered the 10. Baltimore 34, Dallas 31 in Rio - Tyler Loop's 56-yard field goal walked it off. The game-time call went the Ravens' way: Zay Flowers was active after the hamstring injury. Baltimore won but didn't cover the 3.5.
items.takeaway: Two for two on the morning cards.

items.headline: Weather: Monday night is clean
paragraphs: Soldier Field tomorrow night: a high of 71, cooling into the low 60s by the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff, winds 5 to 10 mph, only a slight chance of rain. Nothing that should touch the game.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: What the cards actually say tonight
paragraphs: Balanced is Broncos moneyline at -102 on FanDuel, 0.75 units. The -102 means every $1.02 you risk wins $1. The app has Denver winning about 54 times in 100, which prices out around -3% expected value at medium reliability. That is not a value play, and it doesn't have to be - Balanced answers 'a strong pick without paying too much,' and -102 is about as cheap as a pick gets.

Value is Broncos +1.5 at -120 on DraftKings, 0.75 units. The -120 means every $1.20 you risk wins $1. This is the app's only +EV read on the board, about +0.5% at medium reliability. Denver can win outright or lose by a point and it still cashes.

Hit Rate is empty tonight. The app's contract for that card found no qualifying offer, so there is no card. That's the app saying 'nothing clears the bar' - not a bug, and not a reason to go looking for one yourself.
For your actual stake, the app does the math from your bankroll and staking setting, and it's deliberately conservative. The 0.75 units is the app's sizing language, not a dollar instruction.
items.takeaway: Two Denver bets, two different questions, one empty card.

items.headline: Two cards, one game - read them separately
paragraphs: Both of tonight's plays are on the same game, and they'll often live or die together. A Denver win cashes both. A Rams win by two or more sinks both. That's not the app doubling down - it's two different questions that happened to land on the same team.

Balanced asks for a strong pick without paying too much. Value asks for the model's +EV price. They agree on the team and disagree on the bet: one needs Denver to win outright, the other just needs Denver to keep it within a point.
items.takeaway: Same team, different bets. Score them separately.

items.headline: Sunday evening board: what moved today
paragraphs: Rams at Broncos was the day's move. The Rams went from -130 to -112 on the DraftKings moneyline; Denver went from +110 to -108 (-102 on FanDuel). Pinnacle - the benchmark the app colors its market rows against - sits nearly pick'em at -106/-104. The app's expected-margin number still has the Rams by less than a point. Whatever the cause, the evening cards are priced on the moved number, not the morning one.

Eagles at Bears (Monday): Philadelphia steamed from -3.5 to -4.5 on DraftKings and FanDuel, while Pinnacle never left -3.5. The total ticked down from 42.5 to 41.5. The app's number has Chicago by 1.8 - a six-point gap between the model and the DraftKings/FanDuel price. If your book still shows -3.5, that's a different bet than the -4.5 the board prices.

Once the afternoon games kicked off, the app pulled their prices - the board now only shows numbers for the two games left. And the morning's mover is settled: Seattle went from -7.5 to -8.5 overnight, past the app's 7.74, and Washington won outright 33-31. When the market moves past the model's number, the news is fully priced and then some - the extra point and a half didn't change who won.

The board refreshes at 6 a.m. and 6 p.m. Denver. If your book isn't DraftKings or FanDuel, or it shows a different number than the board, tap Check in the app, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and the evaluator for a bet-or-no-bet verdict on your price. Full re-evaluation, not a blind override.
items.takeaway: Denver and Philadelphia moved. Seattle's move didn't survive the game.

items.headline: Tonight's routine
paragraphs: The 6 p.m. board is the last word before kickoff. Both Denver plays are quoted on the books the app watches - if yours shows a different number, Check it before deciding anything. And the ledger: the morning's two cards both hit, tonight's two are pending. Settlement is manual and the tracker only works if you're honest with yourself - log the winners and the losers, tonight, while it's fresh.
items.takeaway: Check your price. Log your bets.

items.headline: Betting term of the day: steam
paragraphs: Steam is when a bunch of bets hit one side quickly and the line jumps - like Philadelphia going from -3.5 to -4.5 on DraftKings and FanDuel today while Pinnacle never moved off -3.5. You can see the move. You can't see the motive - steam alone doesn't tell you whether it's sharp money or a crowd.

That's why the Fade needs more than a move: a verified tickets-vs-handle split (heavy public tickets one way, heavier dollars the other) plus sharp-book movement the other way. I checked VSiN's board tonight - their splits are DraftKings-only numbers and the per-game tool didn't show usable ticket/handle figures - so there's no verified split and no Fade. The section stays empty rather than forcing one.
items.takeaway: Steam shows the move, not the motive.

evidence.fact: FINAL: New York Giants 12, Tennessee Titans 7 at MetLife Stadium. The nor'easter played out as forecast: rain through the game, driving wind. Jameis Winston started for the Giants (Jaxson Dart out); rookie kicker Dominic Zvada hit all four field goals (27, 30, 39, 39). Cam Ward (23-of-36, 181 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT) drove Tennessee to the Giants' 7 in the final minute but threw an end-zone interception to Jevon Holland with 17 seconds left. The morning brief's Hit Rate and Balanced cards (Giants ML -130) both cashed.
evidence.interpretation: The storm game went to the favorite; the weather was a field-position game as expected.

evidence.fact: FINAL: Las Vegas Raiders 35, New Orleans Saints 27. The morning brief's Value card (Raiders ML +164) cashed. Kirk Cousins threw three touchdowns (22-of-38, 248 yards); Brock Bowers returned from minor knee surgery for his season debut with 10 catches for 116 yards and a touchdown. New Orleans committed four turnovers in the fourth quarter (two Shough strip-sack fumbles, one interception, one Juwan Johnson fumble) after leading 27-16 in the third. Raiders move to 3-0.
evidence.interpretation: The plus-money Value play hit on the back of a fourth-quarter turnover avalanche.

evidence.fact: FINAL: Washington Commanders 33, Seattle Seahawks 31. Marcus Mariota, starting for the injured Jayden Daniels, went 19-of-31 for 183 yards and 3 TDs with no turnovers and sealed it with a late third-down run. Sam Darnold threw for 379 yards and 4 TDs but also 2 interceptions, including a 50-yard pick-six by Kain Medrano in the fourth quarter. Seattle's 12-game winning streak is over. The morning brief noted Seattle had steamed from -7.5 to -8.5 overnight, past the app's expected margin of 7.74.
evidence.interpretation: The market's extra point and a half past the model's number did not change who won.

evidence.fact: FINAL: Kansas City Chiefs 24, Miami Dolphins 10. Patrick Mahomes went 20-of-24 for 246 yards, 2 TDs and 1 INT; Kenneth Walker III scored twice (one rushing, one receiving). Kansas City covered the closing 10. Dolphins RB De'Von Achane injured his knee on Miami's opening drive (3 carries, 17 yards), needed trainers' assistance to leave the field, was initially questionable to return, then ruled OUT late in the second quarter. Malik Willis finished 20-of-36 for 210 yards with an interception. The morning brief noted the app's expected margin had Kansas City by only about 4; the market's -10 was closer to right.
evidence.interpretation: The app's biggest miss of the day; Achane's knee is the injury to watch into Week 4.

evidence.fact: FINAL: Baltimore Ravens 34, Dallas Cowboys 31 in Rio de Janeiro (Maracana). Tyler Loop hit a 56-yard walk-off field goal. The morning's game-time call resolved in Baltimore's favor: WR Zay Flowers (hamstring) was ACTIVE after working out pregame, though his snaps were expected to be limited. Ravens LT Ronnie Stanley (toe) was OUT; DT Nnamdi Madubuike was active. Dallas was without LB DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring), CB Cobie Durant (hamstring), S Malik Hooker (forearm); S P.J. Locke went to injured reserve. Baltimore won but did not cover the 3.5; the morning brief noted the app's expected margin had Dallas by 1.5.
evidence.interpretation: The Ravens survived Rio; the app's Dallas lean was the right side of the number.

evidence.fact: Bears QB Caleb Williams (hamstring) did not practice all week and is OUT for Monday night vs Philadelphia. Tyson Bagent cleared the NFL concussion protocol Saturday, was a full practice participant, and head coach Ben Johnson said he will be available; Bagent is officially listed as questionable but is the expected starter, and the app's expected starter matches (Tyson Bagent, FRESH). 38-year-old Case Keenum - who has not played since 2023 - is the fallback.
evidence.interpretation: Monday night's quarterback question is settled barring a setback.

evidence.fact: Eagles final injury report: TE Dallas Goedert (knee), WR Marquise Brown (ankle), and OT Fred Johnson (knee) are OUT for Monday night at Chicago; OLB Jonathan Greenard (pectoral) is questionable. RB Saquon Barkley (stinger) and WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring) both practiced fully Saturday and carry no game designation - both will play.
evidence.interpretation: Philadelphia gets its lead back and top receiver back but loses three other offensive pieces.
